clinicalPearls: Caused by missense variants clustered in exons 30 and 31 of CREBBP, the gene encoding the histone acetyltransferase CBP, and is regarded as distinct from classic Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome despite involving the same gene
Unlike Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome, it lacks the hallmark broad and often angulated thumbs and great toes
Typical features include short stature, microcephaly, intellectual disability and a characteristic face with short palpebral fissures, telecanthus, a depressed nasal bridge and a short nose
Recurrent upper airway and ear infections and hearing loss are frequently reported
Feeding difficulties, autistic features and behavioural problems are common
The equivalent phenotype arising from variants in the corresponding region of EP300 is designated Menke-Hennekam syndrome type 2

Because the variants affect a specific domain of the acetyltransferase, the disorder illustrates how domain-specific changes in one chromatin modifier can produce a phenotype separate from the classic syndrome
reference.pathophysiology: CREBBP encodes CBP, a histone acetyltransferase and transcriptional co-activator that acetylates histones and numerous non-histone proteins, opening chromatin and coordinating context-dependent gene expression. Whereas most Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome variants cause loss of function across the protein, the missense changes clustered in exons 30 and 31 alter a specific region and are thought to disturb the protein's function in a distinct, possibly localised manner rather than simply reducing its dose. This domain-specific perturbation of acetylation-dependent transcriptional control produces a recognisable pattern of growth restriction, microcephaly, intellectual disability and characteristic facial features that differs from the classic Rubinstein-Taybi phenotype, and an analogous mechanism applies to the EP300-related form.
additionalDifferentials: Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome (classic CREBBP or EP300 variants)
Other syndromic intellectual disability with microcephaly and short stature
additionalInvestigations: Exome or genome sequencing with careful attention to the exon 30-31 region of CREBBP (and EP300)
DNA methylation episignature analysis where available to help classify variants
Evaluation of recurrent infections and airway problems
Neurodevelopmental and behavioural assessment including autism screening
Growth monitoring and evaluation of short stature and microcephaly
redFlags: Recurrent or severe respiratory and ear infections requiring assessment
Feeding difficulty with faltering growth in infancy
Unrecognised hearing loss impairing language development
reference.prognosis: The disorder is generally compatible with survival into adulthood; intellectual disability is usually present and variable in degree, and outcome is aided by treating hearing loss and recurrent infections and by sustained developmental and educational support.
pitfalls: Assuming any CREBBP variant means Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome and thereby misjudging prognosis and management
Discounting the diagnosis because the broad thumbs of Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome are absent
Overlooking treatable hearing loss and recurrent infections
Failing to consider the EP300-related type 2 form in a similar clinical picture
references: GeneReviews — CREBBP/EP300-related disorders and Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome
Nature Reviews — histone acetyltransferases and domain-specific chromatinopathies
management: Symptom-directed care as no disease-specific therapy exists, coordinated through a multidisciplinary team
Audiological management of hearing loss with hearing aids and ENT review
Prompt treatment and prevention of recurrent upper airway and ear infections
Nutritional and feeding support for feeding difficulties with paediatric dietetic input
Early developmental intervention with speech, occupational and physiotherapy plus tailored educational support for intellectual disability
Behavioural support and autism-focused strategies for behavioural difficulties
Growth monitoring with evaluation of short stature and microcephaly
Genetic counselling for the family with confirmation of the CREBBP or EP300 variant
